title: Georgetown and Royal Spring

bodyMarkdown:
Georgetown exists because of one big spring. On July 9, 1774, surveyor [John Floyd](/people/#john-floyd) and his party found a spring so strong that it ran off as a creek of its own. At first it was called "Mr. Floyd's Spring." Floyd claimed a thousand acres around it.

The next autumn a party of Pennsylvanians settled on the bluff above the spring. Among them were [John McClelland](/people/#john-mcclelland) of Westmoreland County and [Robert Patterson](/people/#robert-patterson), who later helped found [Lexington](/stories/col-robert-patterson-builds-lexington/).

Floyd came back in June 1776 meaning to drive McClelland off. Instead, seeing the family, he sold him the land. That summer settlers raised a fort on the bluff. The [National Register nomination](https://npgallery.nps.gov/GetAsset/5b4d8465-e170-4a0e-91c5-5cae501ef582) notes that McClelland's Fort was then one of only four garrisons in Kentucky, with Boonesborough, Logan's, and Harrodsburg.

It did not last. On December 29, 1776, Mingo warriors under [Pluggy](/people/#pluggy) attacked. Pluggy was killed, McClelland was mortally wounded, and [Edward Worthington](/stories/edward-worthington-at-worthingtons-fort/) was among the wounded. The settlers abandoned the station early in 1777.

The spring waited for a builder. Baptist preacher [Elijah Craig](/people/#elijah-craig) came from Virginia and, in 1784, [laid out a town called Lebanon](https://grokipedia.com/page/Georgetown,_Kentucky) on the spring. He opened a classical school in 1787, an ancestor of Georgetown College. He also built mills, a ropewalk, and Kentucky's first paper mill.

Craig is also traditionally credited with aging corn whiskey in charred barrels around 1789, though historians treat that claim with caution. Georgetown still calls itself the "Birthplace of Bourbon."

In 1790 the town was renamed George Town for [George Washington](/people/#george-washington). When Scott County was formed in 1792, the town became its seat.

The spring kept working. It supplied the town's drinking water for generations. Georgetown grew around it into a college town and, since 1988, the home of Toyota's first wholly owned American plant.

## Kentucky today

Royal Spring Park, on West Main Street in downtown Georgetown, has been on the National Register since 1973. Visitors can see the spring, markers for McClelland's Fort and for bourbon, and an 1874 log cabin built by Milton Leach, a formerly enslaved man, moved to the park as a museum.
